ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; notify the driver that an "I'm Here" no-show cancellation requires more than 3 continuous minutes inside the 200 m radius after the tap, and that the pre-tap presence does not count. Do not flag the account.
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case as cancelled_by = driver claiming rider no-show, so the $6.61 passes or falls solely through NS-1/NS-2 [F4]. NS-1 is cumulative: (i) and (ii) plus the continuous post-tap wait in (iii).

NS-1(i) is met — the platform recorded an arrival confirmation, driver_tap at 13:02:35 [F6] — and NS-1(ii) is met, because at that tap the driver was 39 m from the pickup (closest approach overall 38 m), inside the radius [F6][F1]. The GPS trace runs from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no hole, so the waiting period is measurable on system data [F2][F6].

NS-1(iii) fails. The clause counts only continuous waiting at the pickup AFTER the arrival confirmation (the tap), not time spent nearby before it. From the 13:02:35 tap to the 13:05:30 cancellation the driver was continuously inside 200 m for 175 s (2 min 55 s), below the required >180 s (≥3:01) [F6][F4]. The 4 min 30 s inside 200 m from 13:01:00 [F2][F5] and the stationary period 13:02:15–13:05:30 at 40 m [F3] are pre-tap and expressly excluded by NS-1(iii), so they cannot cure the shortfall. At the moment the driver cancelled, only about 2 min 55 s of the required time had elapsed; the 3-minute mark post-tap would have fallen at 13:05:35, five seconds after the cancellation [F4][F6].

Because NS-1(iii) is not satisfied, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full [F7]. The driver's chat message "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" [F10] and his written statement that he waited more than 3 minutes after tapping [F12] are statements; the system records (GPS/timeline) govern where they conflict, and they show 175 s [F4][F6]. The mark is not the tap being outside the radius — it was 39 m — so the NS-2 flag_account limb is not triggered [F6][F1]. The driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days over 772 trips) is not used to decide this case: profile facts cannot decide a case alone, and RD-6 is about route-deviation disputes, which is not the dispute here [F17].

Amount: the cancelled-for item is the cancellation fee on record, $6.61, with no surge (1.0×), so the full sum is refundable [F7][F8]; $6.61 × 1 = $6.61.

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages [F9] ("Reached, blue Toyota Prius, waiting at the pickup.") and [F10] ("More than 3 min already, I have to cancel"), the driver's post-trip statement [F12], and the rider's complaint ("I came out a minute after the driver cancelled. I was charged $6.61 for nothing."). Nothing in these is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are ordinary pickup and cancellation notices and the complaint is a fare grievance. safety_concern = none.

The 38 m closest approach and the stationary period 13:02:15–13:05:30 at 40 m [F1][F3] are pre-tap and are expressly excluded by NS-1(iii), which measures the continuous wait after the arrival confirmation [F6].
The rider's complaint admission is a statement; the charge is determined by the system post-tap clock, which shows 175 s, not by when the rider says she came out [F4][F6].
The framework (NS-0 → NS-1/NS-2, no surge) is correct, but on that framework NS-1(iii) fails, so NS-2 requires full refund rather than no action [F4][F6][F7][F8].
A complete, timestamped chat [F11] does not cure the timing failure; F10's 'More than 3 min already' is a statement contradicted by the system record showing 175 s since the tap [F4][F6].
Conceded and accepted: the tap at 39 m satisfies NS-1(i) and (ii) [F6], but NS-1(iii) is a separate cumulative requirement that fails.
